variants.headline: Building project badly behind schedule
variants.sub: Construction of a building project is severely delayed in {colony}.
variants.body:
A building project is badly behind schedule in {colony}. The delay is the established failure against its timetable, not a complete account of why it occurred. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known position from invented shortages, contractor disputes or financial consequences not supplied in the report.

A severe delay is a delivery issue, not automatically a quantified cost overrun. Managers should distinguish the schedule position from an assumed financial effect. Commercial scrutiny should concern the actual obligations and delivery record, without filling an incomplete account with a guessed penalty, cause or revised completion date.

We fault {target} over the standard of delivery. A schedule is not an ornament to a project, and serious lateness is a proper reason to question the adequacy of the stewardship involved. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.

variants.headline: Construction timetable falls seriously short
variants.sub: A colony building project has fallen badly behind its schedule.
variants.body:

variants.sub: A building project in the colony is badly behind schedule.
variants.body:
